Yes—under those conditions, you’d very likely be able to spot the Moon.

It is high in the sky at about **58° altitude**, well separated from the Sun by **80.9°**, and **42% illuminated**. Although daylight sky brightness reduces contrast, a crescent or half-moon is commonly visible to unaided eyes in a clear blue sky, especially when it is this high and far from the Sun. Its angular size is also normal—roughly **31 arcminutes**—so distance does not make it unusually difficult.

Look generally toward **azimuth 193°** (south-southwest), about **58° above the horizon**—roughly two-thirds of the way from the horizon to overhead. You may find it easiest by first locating it with binoculars or a phone compass/sky app, then looking unaided. Avoid sweeping near the Sun, and never use binoculars or a telescope anywhere near it.
